report:
Dear Colleague,

In the patient's Cranial MRI examination:
Sequences used in the examination:
Axial plane; FLAIR and T2 W FSE,
Sagittal plane; T2 W FSE, 
Coronal plane; T1 W SE. 

The fourth ventricle is of normal size and configuration. Basal cisterns are open. Cerebellar hemispheres, vermis, and brainstem are of normal signal intensity and morphology.

Both internal acoustic canals are of normal width. Sella is of normal shape. Both cavernous sinuses are symmetric and of normal signal intensity.

Convexity sulci are consistent with the patient's age. 
Several millimetric hyperintensities are present in the bilateral periventricular and supraventricular deep white matter, and also patchily in the subcortical white matter, observed on T2 and FLAIR weighted examinations, evaluated as consistent with chronic microangiopathic ischemic gliotic foci. 
                   	
Corpus callosum is of normal signal intensity and morphology. 
Pericallosal pathology was not detected. The ventricular system is of normal width, and the third ventricle is midline. No deviation was observed in midline structures. 

No extra-axial or intra-axial collections or mass lesions were detected.
No findings suggestive of thrombus were detected in the dural sinuses. A 6 mm diameter retention cyst appearance was observed on the anteroinferomedial wall of the right maxillary sinus. Aeration of other paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells is normal.

Impression: -Chronic microangiopathic ischemic gliotic foci observed in the bilateral periventricular and supraventricular deep white matter, and also patchily in the subcortical white matter
	      -6 mm diameter retention cyst in the right maxillary sinus
